name: Optimize effect-heavy code (effects + json codec benchmarks)

description: Baseline: fix tail-resumptive detection + mutable box ParseState handler. effects=33.42ms, json=291.76ms
Replace Mutex with UnsafeCell (MutCell) in MutableBox — negligible improvement (325→324ms)
Eliminate 2 String allocations per Perform: use &str refs instead of .to_string(). effects: 33→31ms, json: 291→289ms
Optimize tail-resumptive Perform: combined handler+entry search, avoid Vec alloc for args, pop directly into locals
Aborting handler fast path: skip continuation capture when handler doesn't use k. JSON: 290→286ms
Global PushGlobal cache: JSON hangs (infinite loop likely from stale cache entry)
Rewrite with-output handler to use mutable box + tail-resumptive. Eliminates all continuation captures during encoding. JSON: 286→256ms (-10.5%)
Re-run of current state for confirmation. 286ms vs 287ms — within noise.
Cache parsed handler descriptors to avoid JSON re-parsing per PushHandler. JSON: 256→226ms (-11.7%)
Convert HandlerEntry effect_name/op_name from String to Arc<str>. No improvement (258 vs 257ms)
Wrap FunctionPrototype in Arc in ConstantValue — closure creation is now refcount bump instead of deep clone. JSON: 226→214ms (-5.5%), effects: 31→30ms
Ultra-fast path for constant-returning tail-resume closures (skip frame push/pop). Negligible impact — JSON closures have upvalues.
Optimize string-char-at: O(1) ASCII fast path using s.is_ascii() + make_some/make_none helpers. Also avoids String alloc for ADT tags.
Effect dispatch table: stale index after CPS handler stack modifications. Too many rebuild sites, overhead offsets gains.
Avoid Vec heap alloc for builtin args (≤4): use stack array in Call and TailCall. Small consistent improvement.
Perform inline cache with handler version counter — massive regression (sed inserted version bumps poorly, causing excessive cache misses)
Perform inline cache with handler version counter (clean implementation). No consistent improvement — single-entry cache thrashes with alternating ops.
Wrap Closure in Arc (CallFrame + VMObject). Regression — Arc::new allocation + indirection overhead > clone savings.
Share HandlerEntries via Arc between VMHandlerFrame and HandlerDispatch. No improvement — entries are small, Arc allocation offsets clone savings.
Optimize json-string-char: peek first to avoid try-parse for non-escaped chars. Eliminates PushHandler/PopHandler per normal string char. JSON: 214→198ms (-7.5%)
Inline JSON bool parsing (avoid try-parse for true/false). Negligible improvement — test JSON only has 1 bool value.
Cache ADT tag strings (Some/None/Ok/Err/Nil/Cons) via LazyLock. No improvement — Rust SSO makes short string clones cheap.
Stack-array for Construct fields (≤4 arity). No improvement — Vec allocator already efficient for small sizes.
Re-run confirmation of current state. JSON 208ms — stable at ~200ms median. No new changes.
PushGlobal resolution cache: cache resolved Value by constant pool pointer, clear on SetGlobal. Avoids HashMap lookup for builtins after warmup. JSON: 200→197ms
Try-take closure ownership in Op::Call to avoid clone. No improvement — closures are usually shared (refcount > 1).
Stack-array for ADT constructor fields. No improvement — .to_vec() same cost as vec! for small sizes.
Fix handle body upvalue capture from grandparent scopes: pre-resolve free vars before snapshot_scope(). Enables inlining try-parse into many-parse.
Inline try-parse into many-parse: handler still reinstalled per iteration (inside recursive go). No improvement.
Trivial tail-resume fast path: [PushConst, Return] with no upvalues/args → push constant directly, skip frame overhead. effects: 31→29ms (-6.8%)
Avoid closure clone for trivial tail-resume (use ref instead). No improvement — empty upvalue Vec clone is already free.
